v2.name: Lab 5 Part C fix -- completeness rule added
v2.single_variable: Rule 7 appended to the shipped lenient prompt. Rules 1-6 byte-identical, verified by diff. The refusal threshold is untouched.

headline.verdict: FLAT ON THE TARGET METRIC, REGRESSIONS ELSEWHERE
headline.predicted: recover 4-6 of 9 partial-credit mode-6 cases; correctness 1.500 -> 1.60-1.70; refusal precision unchanged at ~0.57
headline.measured: correctness 1.500 -> 1.500 (delta 0.0000). Recovered 4 cases but broke 4 previously-passing ones. Refusal recall -0.200, refusal precision -0.143, faithfulness -0.044.

d1_before_after.note: v1 cost not captured in this run; see reports/report4.md. Prompt is 1 rule longer so per-query cost is at most a few percent up, well inside the 2x rule.
v1 p95 not captured in this run; output tokens rose 12%, so p95 should be modestly up.

d2_regression_check.summary: This fix REGRESSED three metrics. The headline delta of 0.0000 is a cancellation of four gains against four losses, not an absence of effect.

regressions.cause: 3 previously-answerable questions became refusals: Q13, Q21, Q42.
7 refusals in v2 but only 4 of them unanswerable. Q36 also stopped refusing, so the denominator grew while the numerator shrank.
Q06 and Q45 each lost faithfulness 1 -> 0 despite identical correctness. Rule 7 asks the model to name a second condition, and it occasionally names one the sources do not support.

improvements.what: Added 'Maternity benefits are only available on the Silver, Gold, and Platinum plans' -- exactly the clause Part A predicted was missing.
Named the second hop that Part A identified as crowded out.
Wrongful refusal resolved. Answered with the 30-day / 15-day instalment split after refusing in v1.
Wrongful refusal resolved. Gave the 200 points and the 1000=5% capped-at-15% conversion.

regressions_by_question.what: Added the archived-2024 15-day policy that the gold answer omits. Faithful to the sources, wrong against the reference. This is the archived-document trap leaking into a single_hop question.
Became a wrongful refusal on a question it answered correctly before. Cost 2 points.
Became a wrongful refusal. Cost 1 point.
Became a wrongful refusal. Cost 2 points.

kinds_already_passing.note: single_hop was the strongest kind in v1 (1.722) and took the worst hit.

d3_reclassification.interpretation: The distribution did NOT shift. All 5 mode-4 (ranking) failures persist untouched, which makes sense: a prompt change cannot fix retrieval. Of the 12 mode-6 failures, 3 recovered and 3 turned into new refusals, leaving 8. This is not a case of revealing a masked problem -- it is a wash in the mode-6 cluster paid for with regressions in refusal behaviour and faithfulness.

d4_next_fix.what: final_k 8 -> 12, targeted at the 5 mode-4 ranking failures.
d4_next_fix.why: It is the only untouched cluster, it is nearly free (no extra model call), and 4 of its 5 cases are aggregation / archived-trap / multi-hop questions where a specific crowded-out fact is the gap.
d4_next_fix.expected_value: 2-3 of 5. Lower than the count suggests, because Q22 and Q35 need a specific document rather than more chunks, and more context on aggregation questions mostly adds distractors.
d4_next_fix.caveat: The cost is latency and prompt tokens rising, and per D2 more context did not cause refusals here -- but this fix has not been tested, so refusal behaviour must be re-measured rather than assumed.

cost_discipline.rule: fix must cost <= 2x the Lab 4 baseline per query
cost_discipline.evidence: The change adds one prompt rule and no model call. v2 cost $0.5138 for 45 questions = $0.0114/query.
